# Local integration changes

`src_v/jpeg_input.v`: handle the AXI-style final-word flag together with the
low-contiguous byte strobes. The original parser treated `inport_last_i` as an
immediate end on the first byte of a word, acknowledging and discarding its
remaining bytes. This loses JPEG EOI for final words containing 2, 3 or 4 bytes.

The local fix derives `input_last_w` at the last asserted strobe and uses it for
byte-index reset, parser retirement, table last flags and word acknowledgement.
Full-word acknowledgement still occurs at byte index 3. The upstream adapter
holds the word, strobes and last flag stable until acknowledgement.

Regression: `../../sim/tb_jpeg_input_tail.v` covers all four byte alignments.
`../../sim/check_frame.py --alignments` additionally compares complete RGB
frames against an independent FFmpeg reference after harmless APP0 padding
shifts EOI alignment. The reference uses nearest-neighbor chroma reconstruction,
as implemented by this core. Approximate integer IDCT errors are reported using
MAE and PSNR; natural-image acceptance requires MAE < 2/255 and PSNR > 40 dB.

Integration 06 instantiates `jpeg_core` with `SUPPORT_WRITABLE_DHT=0`.
The four existing `jpeg_dht_std_*.v` implementations are enabled in the TD
project; they had been marked AutoExcluded when the dynamic branch was used.
The host checker in `tools/jpeg_profile.py` validates all four Annex K tables,
the SOF0/SOS component mapping and absence of restart intervals/multiple scans.
Every frame generated by the packer uses `optimize=False`. All frames in the
CES and existing legacy images pass this profile. This is an integration
simplification for board diagnosis, not evidence that dynamic DHT caused the
observed stall. The core reset is now a registered per-frame signal, rather
than a combinational decode of the pipeline FSM.

Integration 07 fixes stale-byte marker detection during input bubbles. At the
end of a word, byte_idx becomes zero but last_b still contains lane 3 and the
adapter holds the old word while fetching SRAM data. For a word C0 xx xx FF,
the original ungated token decoder sees a synthetic FF C0 while VALID=0 and
clears the frame dimensions. D9 xx xx FF can similarly synthesize an EOI.
All token comparisons now require input VALID. SOF field and length-register
updates require an accepted byte. No error check or watchdog is removed.
`sim/tb_jpeg_input_gaps.v` reproduces dimensions becoming zero before the fix
and retaining 640x480 afterward. The local legacy video's zero-based frame 4
contains the triggering C0/FF word at byte offset 18672; frames 0..3 do not.
